title: Hebrews Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 11.

questions.question: In Hebrews 11, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Faith as the substance of things hoped for
questions.correctAnswer: Faith as the substance of things hoped for
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:1 starts the chapter defining faith as the substance of things hoped for.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 11, what did the elders obtain by faith?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:2 states that by faith the elders obtained a good report.

questions.question: How were the worlds framed according to Hebrews 11?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:3 says the worlds were framed by the word of God.

questions.question: Who offered a more excellent sacrifice to God by faith?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:4 states that by faith Abel offered God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain.

questions.question: What happened to Enoch by faith according to Hebrews 11?
options: He was translated so he should not see death
questions.correctAnswer: He was translated so he should not see death
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:5 explains that by faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death.

questions.question: What is impossible without faith, according to Hebrews 11?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:6 states without faith it is impossible to please God.

questions.question: Who prepared an ark by faith to save his household?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:7 says by faith Noah prepared an ark to save his house.

questions.question: Who was called to go out into a place he should after receive for an inheritance?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:8 relates that Abraham obeyed when called to go to a place for inheritance.

questions.question: With whom did Abraham sojourn in the land of promise?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:9 says Abraham dwelt in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob.

questions.question: What did Abraham look for by faith, according to Hebrews 11?
options: A city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God
A land flowing with milk and honey
questions.correctAnswer: A city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:10 states Abraham looked for a city with foundations built by God.

questions.question: How did Sarah receive strength to conceive a child according to Hebrews 11?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:11 says Sarah received strength to conceive through faith.

questions.question: True or False: The elders obtained a good report by faith.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:2 confirms that by faith the elders obtained a good report.

questions.question: True or False: Noah prepared an ark by faith to save his household.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:7 states Noah prepared an ark by faith to save his house.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 11 says that Abraham received the promises during his lifetime.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:13 says the faithful died not having received the promises, but seeing them afar off.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 11 states that Enoch built the ark and pleased God.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:5 says Enoch pleased God and was translated; Noah built the ark (Hebrews 11:7).

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 11:16, why is God not ashamed to be called their God?
options: Because they desire a better country, even a heavenly one
Because they obey the law perfectly
Because they build temples in His honor
questions.correctAnswer: Because they desire a better country, even a heavenly one
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:16 states that God is not ashamed to be called their God because they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 11:18 promise will happen if Abraham offers up his only begotten son as stated in Hebrews 11:17?
options: His seed will be called in Isaac
He will become king of a great nation
He will live a long life on earth
questions.correctAnswer: His seed will be called in Isaac
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:18 says, 'Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called,' which follows the action of Abraham offering up Isaac in verse 17.

questions.question: What did Abraham believe about God when he offered up Isaac, according to Hebrews 11:19?
options: That God was able to raise him up even from the dead
That God would provide another son
That God would protect Isaac from harm
questions.correctAnswer: That God was able to raise him up even from the dead
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:19 explains that Abraham accounted that God was able to raise Isaac from the dead, which was a figure of the resurrection.

questions.question: How do Hebrews 11:24 and 11:25 connect in describing Moses' choices?
options: Moses refused to be called Pharaoh's son and chose to suffer affliction with God's people
Moses accepted the pleasures of Egypt but later changed his mind
Moses was afraid of Pharaoh's wrath and fled Egypt
Moses sought riches in Egypt before leading the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: Moses refused to be called Pharaoh's son and chose to suffer affliction with God's people
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:24 says Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, and 11:25 shows he chose to suffer affliction with God's people rather than enjoy sin's pleasures.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith can Christians learn from Abraham's example in Hebrews 11:17-19?
options: Faith requires trusting God's promises even in difficult trials
Faith is only about following rituals
questions.correctAnswer: Faith requires trusting God's promises even in difficult trials
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:17-19 shows Abraham offered Isaac trusting God could raise him up, illustrating faith in God’s promises amidst trials.

questions.question: Why did Moses keep the Passover and sprinkle blood according to Hebrews 11:28?
options: To prevent the destroyer of the firstborn from touching the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent the destroyer of the firstborn from touching the Israelites
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:28 explains that Moses kept the Passover and sprinkled blood so the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch those protected by faith.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 11:22 illustrate Joseph's faith regarding the future of Israel?
options: By giving commandment concerning his bones and mentioning the departure of Israel
By building a temple for God
By writing laws for the people
questions.correctAnswer: By giving commandment concerning his bones and mentioning the departure of Israel
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:22 shows Joseph’s faith as he spoke about Israel’s future departure and gave instructions about his bones.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 11:15 teach about those who are mindful of their former country?
options: They might have had opportunity to return
questions.correctAnswer: They might have had opportunity to return
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:15 states that if they had been mindful of their former country, they might have had opportunity to return, indicating the importance of focusing on the promised better country.

questions.question: How did Moses demonstrate faith as an infant according to Hebrews 11:23?
options: He was hid for three months by his parents, who were not afraid of the king's command
He was sent to the palace immediately
He was taken to Egypt by the king
He was abandoned in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: He was hid for three months by his parents, who were not afraid of the king's command
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:23 describes how Moses’ parents hid him for three months by faith, not fearing the king’s command to kill him.

questions.question: What reward did Moses respect that caused him to esteem the reproach of Christ as greater riches according to Hebrews 11:26?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:26 states Moses esteemed the reproach of Christ greater riches than Egyptian treasures because he had respect unto the recompense of the reward.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 11:20 indicate about Isaac's faith in blessing Jacob and Esau?
options: He blessed them concerning things to come
He blessed them for earthly wealth
He cursed them for their sins
questions.correctAnswer: He blessed them concerning things to come
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:20 shows Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau by faith, looking forward to future things.

questions.question: How did Jacob demonstrate faith according to Hebrews 11:21?
options: He blessed the sons of Joseph and worshipped leaning on his staff
questions.correctAnswer: He blessed the sons of Joseph and worshipped leaning on his staff
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:21 describes Jacob's faith as he blessed Joseph’s sons and worshipped while leaning on his staff.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 11:27, Moses endured by faith because he feared the wrath of the king.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:27 says Moses forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king, and endured by faith seeing the invisible God.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 11:6 teaches that without faith it is impossible to please God.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:6 clearly states that without faith it is impossible to please God because one must believe in His existence and rewards.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 11:13, the elders received all the promises during their lifetime.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:13 states that the elders died in faith without receiving the promises but saw them afar off and embraced them.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 11.

questions.question: By faith, who passed through the Red Sea as if on dry land?
questions.explanation: The Israelites passed through the Red Sea as if on dry land, as stated in Hebrews 11:29.

questions.question: What happened to the Egyptians who attempted to cross the Red Sea?
questions.explanation: The Egyptians who attempted to cross were drowned according to Hebrews 11:29.

questions.question: What action did the walls of Jericho take after being encompassed for seven days?
questions.explanation: The walls of Jericho fell down after being compassed about for seven days, as stated in Hebrews 11:30.

questions.question: Who is mentioned as having received the spies with peace?
questions.explanation: Rahab is noted for receiving the spies with peace in Hebrews 11:31.

questions.question: Who are the individuals mentioned alongside Gideon in Hebrews 11:32?
questions.explanation: Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthae, David, Samuel, and the prophets are mentioned in Hebrews 11:32.

questions.question: What did the faithful do according to Hebrews 11:33?
questions.explanation: The faithful subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, and obtained promises as noted in Hebrews 11:33.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'pistis' in Hebrews 11:1 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Pistis' translates to 'faith' in English, as it describes the assurance and conviction in Hebrews 11:1.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Hebrews 11:30 as it describes the walls of Jericho?
questions.explanation: The falling of Jericho's walls foreshadows the power of faith in overcoming obstacles, illustrated in Hebrews 11:30.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with the faith of the harlot Rahab?
questions.explanation: James 2:25 highlights Rahab's faith and her actions, correlating with Hebrews 11:31.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of faith leading to victory over enemies?
questions.explanation: Psalm 44:5 speaks of victory through faith, paralleling the themes in Hebrews 11:33.

questions.question: What comes before Hebrews 11:29?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:28 discusses the Passover, which precedes the mention of the Red Sea crossing in Hebrews 11:29.

questions.question: Who were made strong out of weakness according to Hebrews 11:34?
questions.explanation: Women who received their dead raised to life are mentioned in Hebrews 11:35, indicating strength from weakness.

questions.question: The prophets mentioned in Hebrews 11:32 refer to which period of biblical history?
questions.explanation: The prophets listed are associated with the time of the Judges, as suggested by the context of Hebrews 11:32.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 11:39 states that all the faithful received the promise.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:39 states that these all did not receive the promise, indicating that their faith awaited fulfillment.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 11:40 mentions that God provided something better for the faithful.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:40 confirms that God provided something better for us, ensuring that they would not be made perfect without us.

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 11:6 teach about salvation?
options: Faith is essential to please God and approach Him
Salvation is attained through works of the law
Only knowledge of God is required for salvation
Salvation depends on visible signs and miracles
questions.correctAnswer: Faith is essential to please God and approach Him
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:6 states that without faith it is impossible to please God and that one must believe He exists and rewards those who seek Him, emphasizing faith as essential to salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine promise and human hope does Hebrews 11:13 teach?
options: The faithful die without receiving the promises but trust them in hope
God's promises are always fulfilled in this life
Faithful believers reject hope for heavenly things
Promises are conditional on immediate fulfillment
questions.correctAnswer: The faithful die without receiving the promises but trust them in hope
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:13 explains that those who lived by faith died without receiving the promises, but they saw them from afar and embraced them, showing trust in the hope of God's promises.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty and human obedience does Hebrews 11:8 teach?
options: Faith involves obeying God’s call even without knowing the outcome
Obedience requires full knowledge of the future
questions.correctAnswer: Faith involves obeying God’s call even without knowing the outcome
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:8 describes Abraham’s faith in obeying God's call to go to an unknown place, illustrating human obedience under divine sovereignty without full knowledge of the future.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 11:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:3 states that the worlds were framed by the word of God, showing God’s sovereign power in creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 11:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:17 shows Abraham’s faith in offering Isaac, a demonstration of God’s faithfulness to keep His promises despite testing.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 11:29 connect to the broader redemptive-historical theme of deliverance in Scripture?
options: It prefigures the ultimate deliverance through Christ’s resurrection
It rejects the concept of divine intervention in history
It focuses solely on physical liberation without spiritual meaning
It contradicts the deliverance theme in the Old Testament
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the ultimate deliverance through Christ’s resurrection
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:29 recounts the crossing of the Red Sea by faith, which typologically points to Christ’s redemptive work delivering believers from sin and death.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Hebrews 11:31 establish with the inclusion of Rahab?
options: God’s grace extends to Gentiles who demonstrate faith
Salvation is limited to ethnic Israel only
Faith is unnecessary for inclusion in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God’s grace extends to Gentiles who demonstrate faith
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:31 highlights Rahab, a Gentile harlot, who was saved by faith, demonstrating the expansion of God's covenant to include faithful Gentiles.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 11:1 and Hebrews 11:3 teach about faith and creation?
options: Faith perceives unseen realities and accepts God’s sovereign creative word
Faith is irrelevant to understanding creation
Creation is self-existent and independent of faith
Faith only applies to salvation, not to creation
questions.correctAnswer: Faith perceives unseen realities and accepts God’s sovereign creative word
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:1 defines faith as assurance of unseen things and Hebrews 11:3 reveals faith’s role in understanding that God created all things by His word, emphasizing faith’s function in grasping divine creation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 11:6 and Hebrews 11:27 teach about faith’s object and its effects?
options: Faith requires believing in God’s existence and rewards, leading to fearless endurance
Faith is based on empirical evidence and visible outcomes
Faith causes fear of God’s wrath rather than confidence
Faith is a human achievement independent of God’s character
questions.correctAnswer: Faith requires believing in God’s existence and rewards, leading to fearless endurance
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:6 teaches faith as belief in God’s existence and rewarder nature, and 11:27 shows Moses’ fearless endurance by faith, seeing the invisible God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 11:39 and Hebrews 11:40 teach about the fulfillment of God’s promises?
options: God’s promises were not fully received by the faithful but are perfected together with us
God’s promises were fully realized by all the Old Testament saints
Faithful believers receive promises only in this life
God’s promises are conditional on human perfection
questions.correctAnswer: God’s promises were not fully received by the faithful but are perfected together with us
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:39 states the faithful did not receive the promises fully, and 11:40 explains God provided something better so that they and we might be made perfect together.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Hebrews 11:35-38 teaches that God endorses suffering and persecution. What does these verses actually teach?
options: The verses testify to the faith and endurance of believers amid suffering, not God’s endorsement of suffering
These verses command believers to seek out suffering as a virtue
The verses teach that suffering is always a sign of God’s rejection
The passage argues that faith eliminates all suffering
questions.correctAnswer: The verses testify to the faith and endurance of believers amid suffering, not God’s endorsement of suffering
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:35-38 recounts the trials believers endured by faith, showing their perseverance, not that God desires suffering but that faith sustains through it.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 11:7 teach about human response to divine revelation and judgment?
options: Faith leads to obedience to God’s warning and judgment, resulting in righteousness
Human response has no effect on divine judgment
Judgment occurs regardless of faith or obedience
Faith is irrelevant to salvation in times of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Faith leads to obedience to God’s warning and judgment, resulting in righteousness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:7 shows Noah’s faith in heeding God’s warning to build the ark, which saved his family and condemned the unbelieving world, highlighting faith’s role in judgment and salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 11:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:10 describes Abraham looking for a city built by God, reflecting God’s covenant faithfulness in preparing a heavenly inheritance for His people.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 11:24 and Hebrews 11:25 teach about sanctification and the values of the believer?
options: Sanctification involves choosing suffering with God’s people rather than temporary sinful pleasures
Sanctification is achieved through worldly success and comfort
Believers should avoid all suffering at any cost
Sanctification requires isolation from the people of God
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves choosing suffering with God’s people rather than temporary sinful pleasures
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:24-25 recount Moses’ choice to suffer affliction with God’s people rather than enjoy sin’s pleasures, illustrating sanctification by valuing God’s reward over worldly gain.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 11:22 contribute to the narrative arc of God’s providence and promise fulfillment?
options: Joseph’s faith in instructing about Israel’s departure shows trust in God's providential plan
Joseph’s actions were independent of God’s providence
God’s promises are fulfilled only in the present life
God’s providential care ends with the patriarchs
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph’s faith in instructing about Israel’s departure shows trust in God's providential plan
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:22 shows Joseph’s faith in making provision for Israel’s future, demonstrating trust in God’s ongoing providential plan for His people.
